model: 48/50K and 48/50V Applied Rooftop (SmartVu software 4.X network points)
applies_to: Carrier 48/50K and 48/50V applied rooftop units with PIC 6.1 hardware and SmartVu controls running software version 4.X.
summary: With software 4.X the applied rooftop SmartVu controller publishes a network points list of 129 analog values (configurations, setpoints, BACnet-specific points such as air source linkage and schedule objects, sensors and status) plus 231 binary values in a separate alarm list (one BV per alarm code, with alarm reset and alarm activate). BACnet MS/TP runs on serial port J7 or J8 and BACnet IP on the Ethernet port; only one of CCN or BACnet can be used at a time.
notes: This list is for software 4.X and uses different instances from our earlier 48/50K and 48/50V SmartVu list (48-50-ART-SVU-1T); only about 37 of the 129 analog values share an instance with it.

The table pages are printed rotated; analog values come from Appendix A (BACnet and CCN Network Points) and binary values from Appendix B (Alarms List). Points with no separate BACnet object name use the printed name.
Access is from the WRITE? column (Yes = writable). Enumerations are kept in the states field as printed (e.g. 0=CLEAN, 1=DIRTY). All Appendix B points are BVs; unless noted 0 = NORMAL and 1 = ALARM.
Not all points exist on every unit; availability depends on model, size and options. Software before 2.4.0 uses different instances and names.
Analog value enumerations are kept in the states field as printed (e.g. 0=OFF ... 8=MAX for the component state points).

source.title: Applied Rooftop Units with PIC 6.1 Hardware and SmartVu Controls Version 4.X - Integration Guide (Appendix A, BACnet and CCN Network Points; Appendix B, Alarms List)

integration.summary: Set the J7/J8 serial port (MS/TP) or the IP settings from the SmartVu touchscreen, reboot, then write the network occupancy point after every power cycle and keep network sensor inputs refreshed within the network input timeout. Map the operating mode, occupancy source and filter status, and poll the alarm BVs or Alarm Activate.

minimum_points.name: GENUNIT_NETOCC
minimum_points.why: Network occupancy command (rewrite after power cycle)

minimum_points.name: MDESTS_OP_STATE
minimum_points.why: Operating mode (free, mech, staged, heating, dehum...)

minimum_points.name: STATES_OCCSRNUM
minimum_points.why: Occupancy source in effect (local, BMS, remote...)

integration.enable: The network occupancy point must be written after every controller power cycle to set the unit occupied; otherwise it defaults to not used, which leaves the unit unoccupied. It does not time out and keeps its last value if communication is lost.
integration.heartbeat: Network inputs must be written at least every 10 minutes (service configurable) and after a power cycle; if no write arrives, the unit falls back to its local sensor value if one exists.
integration.remote_sensors: Sensor values can come from network points (including airside linkage); the touchscreen hides a sensor when its local input is disabled unless set to show it.
setup: J7 can be CCN or BACnet MS/TP (factory wired to the CCN comm board); J8 can be BACnet MS/TP or Rnet.
Only one BAS protocol (CCN or BACnet) at a time; most configuration changes need a reboot.
Excel versions of the network points are in the software download file on HVACPartners.
gotchas: Software versions before 2.4.0 use different point instances and names; confirm the controller software version first.
The 4.X list differs from earlier SmartVu lists; do not reuse an older point map without checking instances.

note: Provided as-is. Point availability varies by firmware and options; verify against the live device.
